title: Access scoping patterns by deployment and evidence roadmap
summary: Working playbook: concrete scoping patterns for Hosted / Dedicated / Private environments, a compact role-to-permission matrix, suggested policy templates, recommended audit schema for SIEM export, and a prioritized evidence automation roadmap.
content:
Purpose This doc collects practical access scoping patterns and an evidence automation roadmap for the three deployment tiers (Hosted, Dedicated, Private). Goal: give platform, infra, and product teams fast, repeatable knobs to provision least-privilege access while producing machine-readable evidence that maps to compliance artifacts and SIEM ingest expectations. Notes about scope and audience - Audience: eng infra, SRE, platform security, compliance engineering, and solutions engineering who onboard customers. - Not a final policy; a playbook of recommended patterns and templates for RBAC v2 rollout and evidence exports. - Emphasizes repeatability: service account naming, claim scaffolding, event field contracts for SIEM. Design principles (short) 1) Principle of explicit intent: roles express what the principal may do, not where they do it. Use additional scoping (resource tags, project ids) for environment separation. 2) Fail-safe defaults: deny-by-default for new roles; elevate with timeboxed grants. 3) Evidence-first: every policy change should emit an evidence bundle (who, what, where, when, why) recorded in the evidence store and optionally forwarded to SIEM. 4) Customer isolation: Dedicated and Private must support tenant-scoped roles separate from Redwood-engine roles. High-level role families (RBAC v2) - infra-admin: full deployment lifecycle (create/terminate nodes, manage autoscale, upgrade runtime images) — narrow to internal infra team and designated on-call. - svc-owner: service-level owners that can manage config, secrets, routing for a specific service. Scoped by service: svc-owner:console, svc-owner:batch-ingest. - model-deployer: can upload models, create revisions, initiate canary rollouts; needs strong audit tracking. - read-only-observer: view-only access to dashboards, traces, and audit logs (for auditors, SOC). - billing-analyst: view and export billing and token-level usage; cannot change quotas or configs. - customer-admin (tenant-scoped): for Dedicated/Private, admin within customer boundary (create user accounts, configure routes). - emergency-breakglass: time-limited, heavily audited, requires multi-party approval. Compact IAM matrix (permissions examples) Each row is role -> representative permissions (expressed as capability labels for templates): - infra-admin -> compute.instance.create, compute.instance.delete, infra.cluster.update, network.route.modify, secret.kms.manage - svc-owner -> service.config.read, service.config.write, secret.access:service/*, route.modify:service/* - model-deployer -> model.upload, model.tag, rollout.create, rollout.cancel, model.metrics.read - read-only-observer -> dashboards.view, logs.search, traces.view, audit.events.read - billing-analyst -> billing.view, usage.export, quotas.read - customer-admin -> tenant.user.manage, tenant.policy.apply, tenant.billing.view - emergency-breakglass -> elevated.* (granted via ephemeral token flow only) Environment-specific scoping patterns 1) Hosted (multi-tenant Redwood-managed) - Default posture: central Redwood control plane with tenant-scoped resource identifiers. - Roles: 'svc-owner' and 'model-deployer' are tenant-scoped; infra-admin remains Redwood-internal. - Resource tags: every tenant resource must carry tenant_id, region, and compliance_level tags for automated evidence correlation. - Policy template pattern: use parameterized templates referencing tenant_id and allowed service namespaces. - Evidence: on model.upload, emit event with fields: event_type, actor_id, actor_role, tenant_id, model_id, artifact_hash, ip_origin, request_id. These must be forwarded to SIEM within 1 minute. 2) Dedicated (customer-dedicated capacity, Redwood-managed infra) - Default posture: stronger separation — dedicated compute pools and tenant-scoped service accounts. - Roles: create two classes per role family: redwood_ (infra ops) and tenant_ (customer delegated). - Network boundary: dedicated VPC per customer; network-level rules used as secondary enforcement. - Policy templates: restrict 'tenant_' to resources with label:customer_id==. - Evidence: additionally capture node_pool_id and capacity_commitment_id in events. Evidence export should be retained for configurable retention per contract (default 90 days). 3) Private (customer-managed control plane or on-prem) - Default posture: customer owns control plane; Redwood provides policy bundles and evidence exporters. - Roles: provide local equivalents with guidance; e.g., 'redwood-support-limited' role for remote support (GRANT via explicit support session with timebox). - Trust model: assume local IAM is authoritative; Redwood templates must be mappable to local role claims. - Evidence: support push/pull exporters (S3, syslog, OTLP) and provide a local SIEM schema adapter. Policy template examples (short snippets, replace tokens)
-- service-owner-template -- allow: ["service.config.read","service.config.write","secret.access"] resources: ["service://${tenant_id}/${service_name}/*"] conditions: ["request.from_cidr == ${customer_cidr}", "time.window != night" /* example */] -- model-deployer-template -- allow: ["model.upload","model.tag","rollout.create"] resources: ["models:${tenant_id}:*"] obligations: ["emit_event:true","require_deploy_approval:canary_threshold>1%"] Evidence schema recommendations (fields for SIEM export) Top-level event fields (strings unless noted): - event_id - timestamp (ISO 8601) - event_type (model.upload, policy.change, role.grant, secret.access, login.success, login.failure, breakglass.open) - actor_id (user or service account) - actor_principal_type (human|service|support_session) - actor_role - tenant_id (nullable for infra events) - deployment_tier (hosted|dedicated|private) - resource_type (model, service, node, secret, policy) - resource_id - request_id - ip_origin - geo (country) - outcome (success|failure) - change_summary (short free text) - evidence_refs (comma-separated list of evidence ids) - retention_policy_tag (string, e.g., compliance:hipaa:7yrs) Hints for SIEM mapping - Map event_type to SIEM category and set event.id = event_id. - Use tenant_id as a top-level asset tag. - Normalize actor_role to canonical role families for correlation rules. - Include request latency and token consumption as numeric strings for anomaly detection (optional fields). Evidence automation roadmap (prioritized) 1) Q1: Emit standardized JSON artifact for every policy change and model upload; store in evidence-bucket with naming: /evidence/${tenant_id}/${YYYY}/${MM}/${event_id}.json. Hook lifecycle: policy_change -> evidence_saver -> siem_forwarder. 2) Q2: Implement ephemeral elevated access (breakglass) workflow: approval via 2FA and automatic evidence capture + mandatory postmortem. 3) Q3: Build SIEM field normalization layer and configurable forwarding to Splunk/Datadog/Elastic. 4) Q4: Support on-prem adapter for Private deployments (push to customer endpoint or S3 with pre-signed URL). Open questions & TODOs (working list) - How do we represent composite roles (e.g., model-deployer + billing-analyst) in the token claims so that audits don't explode? (TODO: canonical role array semantics) - Retention policy enforcement for Dedicated customers with differing contractual SLOs — need per-customer retention tags in evidence store. - Breakglass approval UX: integrate approvals into Console -> review offline before autosignature? (Rana to design mock). - Create test harness for SIEM exports with synthetic events (Liam). Implementation notes for SRE/Platform - Standardize service account naming: svc-${team}-${env}-${purpose} e.g., svc-modelinfra-prod-deployer. - Every policy change must create a change-ticket (Jira) and reference it in change_summary and linked_artifacts. - Provide a lightweight CLI to generate policy templates with replaced tokens: ./policy-gen --role=model-deployer --tenant=acme --out=./policies/acme-model-deployer.json Appendix: sample evidence JSON (conceptual) { "event_id": "evt-20250211-7b9f", "timestamp": "2025-02-11T18:24:12Z", "event_type": "model.upload", "actor_id": "user:liam.chen@redwood.ai", "actor_role": "model-deployer", "tenant_id": "acme-corp", "deployment_tier": "dedicated", "resource_type": "model", "resource_id": "models:acme:llama-13b-v2", "request_id": "req-71a2", "ip_origin": "52.14.32.9", "outcome": "success", "change_summary": "initial upload for evaluation build", "evidence_refs": "s3://evidence-bucket/acme/2025/02/evt-20250211-7b9f.json", "retention_policy_tag": "compliance:standard:90d" } (above example for illustration; actual artifact must be emitted as a single-line JSON object and stored with integrity hash) Contact & next steps - Primary owner: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai) — coordinate with Rana (product), Liam (SRE) for Q1 delivery. - Next review: schedule security working session (calendar invite) and collect feedback on the compact role matrix. End of draft.
